source_refs.note: Step 4: Repeating the Cycle: a main subheading of 20.3.1 Steps of PCR, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 161-162.

blocks.text: Steps 1 to 3 are repeated and the two copies become four. It is not necessary to add any more polymerase, as the heating does not harm this enzyme. Each cycle is completed in one or two minutes and it doubles the number of DNA molecules. After 20 cycles, a single fragment of DNA produces more than one million copies.

blocks.alt: A vertical flow. A double-stranded DNA with the gene of interest and free primers (P). Heat: 1- Denaturation separates the strands. Cool: 2- Annealing, a primer P binds to each strand. DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) and free nucleotides added: 3- Extension builds new strands, giving 2 copies (Cycle 1). Heat and cool again give 4 copies (Cycle 2), then 8 copies (Cycle 3). Old strands are blue, new strands red; the two original strands stay in two of the copies.
blocks.caption: Figure 20.6: Steps of PCR (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 20.6).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Gene of interest, Primers, Heat, Cool, 1- Denaturation, 2- Annealing, DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) & Free nucleotides added, 3- Extension, 2 copies, 4 copies, 8 copies, Cycle 1, Cycle 2, Cycle 3.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 20.6 shows an original (parent) strand in three of the eight copies after cycle 3. There are only two parent strands, so only two of the eight copies carry one, as drawn above.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: PCR is also used to build genomic library. It is the collection of the total DNA from a single organism. Genomic libraries are commonly used for sequencing the DNA.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The Taq polymerase is a temperature-tolerant enzyme isolated from Thermus aquaticus, a bacterium found in hot springs. This enzyme is stable and active at near-boiling temperatures.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The optimum temperature for carrying out the extension of primer is 72°C. This step is completed in just one minute.
